title: Factors & Multiples
description: Class 4 IMO — Factors and multiples: prime and composite numbers, divisibility rules for 2, 3, 5 and 10, common multiples, and HCF and LCM by listing.

topics.title: Factors, Prime & Composite Numbers
topics.concept:
A factor of a number divides it exactly with no remainder. The factors of 12 are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6 and 12. Every number has 1 and itself as factors.

A prime number has exactly two factors — 1 and itself (2, 3, 5, 7, 11…). A composite number has more than two factors (4, 6, 8, 9…). The number 1 is neither prime nor composite.

examples.problem: Is 7 a prime or composite number?
examples.solution: Prime — its only factors are 1 and 7.

recap: A factor divides a number exactly.
Prime = exactly two factors; composite = more than two.

quiz.q: Which of these is a prime number?
quiz.explanation: 11 has only the factors 1 and 11, so it is prime.
The factors of 6 are 1, 2, 3 and 6 — that is 4 factors.

topics.title: Multiples & Divisibility Rules
topics.concept:
A multiple is what you get by multiplying a number by 1, 2, 3, and so on. The multiples of 4 are 4, 8, 12, 16, 20…

Divisibility rules help us check quickly: a number is divisible by 2 if it ends in an even digit, by 5 if it ends in 0 or 5, by 10 if it ends in 0, and by 3 if the sum of its digits is divisible by 3.

examples.problem: Write the first three multiples of 6.

examples.solution: Digit sum 1 + 2 + 3 = 6, which is divisible by 3, so yes.

quiz.q: Which number is a multiple of 7?

quiz.explanation: 250 ends in 0, so it is divisible by 10.

topics.title: HCF & LCM by Listing
topics.concept:
The HCF (Highest Common Factor) of two numbers is the largest factor they share. List the factors of each and pick the biggest common one. The factors of 12 are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12 and of 18 are 1, 2, 3, 6, 9, 18 — the HCF is 6.

The LCM (Lowest Common Multiple) is the smallest multiple they share. The first common multiple of 4 and 6 is 12, so the LCM is 12.

examples.solution: Common factors are 1, 2, 4; the highest is 4.
The smallest common multiple of 3 and 4 is 12.

quiz.q: What is the HCF of 6 and 9?
quiz.explanation: Common factors of 6 and 9 are 1 and 3; the highest is 3.

quiz.q: What is the LCM of 2 and 5?
quiz.explanation: The smallest common multiple of 2 and 5 is 10.

questions.q: Which is the odd one out (three are prime numbers)?
questions.explanation: 9 = 3 × 3 is composite; the others are prime.

questions.q: Which number is a factor of 20?

questions.explanation: Digit sum of 27 is 2 + 7 = 9, which is divisible by 3.
The factors of 10 are 1, 2, 5 and 10 — that is 4.

questions.q: Which of these is a composite number?
questions.explanation: 9 has factors 1, 3 and 9, so it is composite.

questions.q: What is the HCF of 12 and 16?
questions.explanation: Common factors are 1, 2, 4; the highest is 4.

questions.q: What is the LCM of 4 and 6?
questions.explanation: The smallest common multiple of 4 and 6 is 12.

questions.q: 24 chocolates are packed in equal groups. Which group size will NOT work (leaves some over)?
questions.explanation: 5 is not a factor of 24, so groups of 5 leave some over.

questions.q: Two bells ring every 4 minutes and 6 minutes. After how many minutes do they ring together?
questions.explanation: They ring together at the LCM of 4 and 6, which is 12 minutes.

questions.q: Two ribbons of 12 m and 18 m are cut into equal pieces of the greatest possible length. What is that length?
questions.explanation: The greatest length is the HCF of 12 and 18, which is 6 m.

questions.q: What is the smallest number that is divisible by both 3 and 4?
Which number between 20 and 30 is a prime number?
questions.explanation: 23 has only the factors 1 and 23, so it is prime.
